## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized wood-decay mushroom characterized by fan-shaped, whitish to grayish caps with a hairy surface and distinctive split-looking gills underneath. In Florida, it is found on dead branches, logs, stumps, and weakened wood in forests, hammocks, swamps, parks, yards, and other humid wooded habitats. It helps decompose dead wood and recycle nutrients, often growing in overlapping clusters that dry out and rehydrate after rain.
